items.text: For explaining individual life outcome differences, the primary factor is:

options.B: Genetics weighted more heavily than environment
options.C: Roughly equal parts nature and nurture
options.D: Environment and upbringing weighted more heavily

items.text: Two children adopted into the same loving, wealthy family—one thrives, one struggles with addiction. The most likely explanation:

options.A: Genetic differences in temperament and vulnerability
options.B: Primarily genetics with some environmental interaction
options.C: Complex interaction of genes, environment, and chance
options.D: Different experiences within the same family environment
options.E: Subtle differences in how each child was treated

items.text: The "blank slate" view (humans shaped entirely by environment) vs. evolutionary psychology (much behavior is innate). Which better explains human behavior?

options.A: Evolutionary psychology—most behavior has innate roots
options.B: Evolutionary psychology captures more, but environment matters
options.C: Both frameworks are needed—neither alone suffices
options.D: Blank slate captures more, but some instincts are innate
options.E: Blank slate—humans are fundamentally shaped by experience
